q: 1. For quality control of portland cement, the test essentially done is
explain: Quality control of Portland cement requires testing setting time, soundness, tensile/compressive strength, and consistency, hence all of these are essential.

q: 2. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the hydration reaction and thereby decreasing the setting time of cement.

q: 3. Slag cement is used is
explain: Slag cement, having moderate heat of hydration and good resistance properties, is commonly used for abutments among the given options.

q: 4. The cement, widely used in retaining walls, is
explain: Retaining walls are mass concrete structures where controlling heat of hydration to avoid thermal cracking is important, so low heat cement is preferred.

q: 5. Di-calcium silicate (C2S)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C2S hydrates slowly and generates less heat of hydration compared to C3S, but contributes to good ultimate strength over a longer period.

q: 6. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S cause rapid hardening
high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S make the cement less resistive to chemical attack
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S contribute to slow hardening
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S provide greater resistance to chemical attack
explain: All the statements correctly describe the relationship between C3S/C2S proportions and hardening rate/chemical resistance of cement.

q: 7. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the compressive strength test of cement mortar, the water content used is (P/4 + 3%) of the combined weight of cement and sand, as specified by IS code, matching option c's form (P + 3% of water).

q: 8. Hardening of cement occurs at
options: rapid rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a decreased rate
slow rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a rapid rate
explain: Cement hardens rapidly in the initial days due to fast hydration of C3S and C3A, then the rate of strength gain slows down over time.

q: 9. The aggregate which pass through 75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 4.75 mm IS sieve is known as
explain: Aggregate passing 75mm sieve but retained on 4.75mm sieve is classified as coarse aggregate as per standard aggregate size classification.

q: 10. Initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS 4031/IS 269, the minimum initial setting time specified for OPC is 30 minutes.

q: 11. Bulk specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, including the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Bulk specific gravity is defined as the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its total (bulk) volume, which includes the natural pores within the particles.

q: 12. The aggregate which passes through 75 mm IS sieve and is entirely retained on 4.75 mm IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve (and passing 75 mm) are classified as coarse aggregate as per standard grading definitions.

q: 13. The maximum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: Fine aggregate is defined as material passing through the 4.75 mm IS sieve, making 4.75 mm its maximum particle size.

q: 14. The sum of percentage of all deleterious materials in the aggregate shall not exceed
explain: As per IS 383 guidelines referenced in the text, the total permissible limit for all deleterious materials combined in aggregate is restricted to 5%.

q: 15. In order to obtain the best workability of concrete, the preferred shape of aggregate is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and least interlocking/friction, which gives the best workability for a given water-cement ratio.

q: 16. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
explain: By definition, an aggregate is classified as flaky when its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5th (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

q: 17. The approx. ratio of direct tensile strength to flexural strength is
explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5) of its flexural strength (modulus of rupture), since flexural tests measure extreme fiber stress differently from direct tension.

q: 18. The concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is essentially a composite material composed mainly of cement, sand, and aggregate (along with water), hence all of the above is correct.

q: 19. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the typical approximate composition by percentage follows the order Lime : Silica : Alumina : Iron oxide as 63 : 22 : 6 : 3.

q: 20. The compressive strength of concrete determined from 150 mm × 150 mm cylinder as compared to that determined from 150 mm cube is
explain: Cylinder specimens generally record lower compressive strength than cube specimens of comparable size due to differences in the stress distribution and end-restraint effects during testing.

q: 21. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: Once cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration reactions begin prematurely within the bag/storage, forming lumps and losing its binding property, rendering it unfit for use.

q: 22. To hydrate 500 kg cement fully, weight of water needed, is
explain: Using the practical full-hydration water requirement of roughly 0.25-0.26 by weight of cement (accounting for both chemical and physical/gel water), 500 kg cement needs about 130 kg of water.

q: 23. The bulk density of aggregate doesn't depend upon
explain: Bulk density is a material property governed by aggregate size, shape, grading, and specific gravity — it is independent of the size or shape of the container used to measure it.

q: 24. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work, is:
options: 15 days for bottom slabs 4.6 m and more
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: Standard formwork removal periods for ordinary cement concrete vary by member: about 2 days for columns, 7 days for beam soffits, and 15 days for larger slabs, so all these apply.

q: 25. On a grading curve, the gap grading is represented by
explain: Gap grading, where certain intermediate particle sizes are missing from the aggregate mix, appears as a horizontal (flat) segment on a standard grading curve.

q: 26. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately
explain: As given in this text, the void content within a mass of cement particles (loose powder) is approximately 25%.

q: 27. Setting time of cement increases by adding
explain: Gypsum is added specifically to retard the rapid setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate, thereby increasing the overall setting time of cement.

q: 28. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Well-graded aggregates, containing a proper distribution of particle sizes, minimize void content and ensure denser, higher quality concrete.

q: 29. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat of hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very rapidly with water, is largely responsible for the initial setting behaviour of cement, and generates a large amount of heat of hydration — all of these properties apply.

q: 30. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: A cement rich in C3S and low in C2S hardens rapidly, develops high early strength, and generates high heat of hydration — all these characteristics occur together.

q: 31. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, premature hydration and lump formation occur, rendering the cement useless for construction.

q: 32. The quality of cement is tested by
explain: Compressive strength testing of standard mortar cubes is the primary and most common method used to assess and certify the quality of cement.

q: 33. The degree of grinding of cement is called
explain: Fineness of cement refers directly to the degree to which the clinker has been ground into fine powder.

q: 34. Too much fineness of cement
explain: Very fine cement hydrates faster, generating more heat of hydration, which can lead to thermal cracking in concrete — so both effects (a and b) occur.

q: 35. Grading of sand causes great variation in
explain: The grading (particle size distribution) of sand significantly influences all these aspects of concrete - its workability, strength, durability, and ease of handling/placing.

q: 36. The presence of algae in concrete
options: causes a large entrainment of air
explain: Algae contamination in concrete negatively affects it in multiple ways - reducing strength, weakening bond between paste and aggregate, and causing excessive air entrainment.

q: 37. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

q: 38. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate particles larger than 75 mm are classified as cyclopean aggregate, typically used in mass concrete works such as dams.

q: 39. If the depth of moist sand in cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of sand when fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the sand is
40. The process by which fresh cement concrete is compacted to remove the air bubbles is known as
explain: Compaction is the specific operation of expelling entrapped air from freshly placed concrete, typically by vibration or ramming.

q: 41. The rock which is not calcareous is
explain: Laterite is an iron/aluminium-rich residual soil/rock formed by weathering, not a calcium-carbonate (calcareous) rock like limestone or chalk.

q: 42. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage is due to its
explain: Rapid hardening cement achieves its high early strength mainly through finer grinding, which increases the surface area available for rapid hydration reaction.

q: 43. Light weight concrete is prepared by
options: formation of air void in concrete by omitting sand
formation of air voids in cement paste by the substances causing foam
explain: Light weight concrete can be produced using lightweight aggregates, by omitting fine aggregate (no-fines concrete), or by introducing air voids through foaming agents — all these are recognized methods.

q: 44. To obtain a light weight concrete the types of aggregate used is
explain: Pumice is a naturally occurring porous, low-density volcanic aggregate commonly used to produce light weight concrete.

q: 45. The interval for which the cement products remain in plastic condition is known as::
explain: Setting time refers to the period during which the cement paste remains workable/plastic before it begins to stiffen and lose plasticity.

q: 46. To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
explain: The standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test specimen for concrete is a beam of size 150 x 150 x 700 mm as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 47. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reactions and therefore mainly boosts early-age strength development rather than the ultimate strength.
